evidence: app/package.json:8 — direct dependency on nitro ^3.0.260903-beta, a pre-release of Nitro v3 (project's own README: 'For the current stable release, see Nitro v2'; npm latest is 3.0.261029-rc)
app/vite.config.ts:2,7 — nitro()/nitro-vite plugin wires the production server, so the pre-stable dep sits in a central place
app/package.json:5 — @solidjs/start ^2.1.0, current stable but released 2026-10-22 (github.com/solidjs/solid-start releases), i.e. very recently stable
app/src/lib/queries.ts:1-43 — query/createAsync/'use server', all long-stable documented Router 1.0 APIs
app/src/entry-server.tsx:25 — createHandler { mode: 'async' } is a documented stable handler option (docs.solidjs.com createHandler reference)
reach.rationale: Exactly one pre-stable dependency (Nitro 3 beta) in a central place — the production server runtime — plus very-recently-stable framework versions; all application-level code uses long-stable APIs.

evidence: app/vite.config.ts:1-9 — the entire Nitro surface is one import and one plugin registration; no presets, no nitro top-level options, no API routes
app/src/lib/queries.ts:4-43 — all server-function access funneled through a single query module with 'use server' wrappers, so app code never touches the server runtime directly
app/src/lib/server/pokeapi.ts:17-54 — plain fetch with an in-memory cache; no Nitro/unstorage/h3 APIs used anywhere in src/
containment.rationale: The pre-stable piece is isolated to two files (package.json and vite.config.ts) and zero Nitro-specific API calls; swapping the deployment plugin would be a two-line change.

evidence: app/vite.config.ts:7 — solidStart() + nitro() is verbatim the documented SolidStart v2 setup (docs.solidjs.com/solid-start/v2/guides/deployment-plugins: 'Nitro v3 supports multiple deployment targets through presets… Add nitro() after solidStart()')
app/package.json:9 — 'start': 'node .output/server/index.mjs' needs a portable node-server build; Nitro v3 is the only generic (non-Netlify/Cloudflare) deployment plugin SolidStart v2 documents
app/src/entry-server.tsx:3-5 — the one non-default option ({ mode: 'async' }) is chosen deliberately for a spec-driven reason (complete HTML for fragment links) and commented
justification.rationale: The single pre-stable dependency is the framework's own prescribed production-server path — no stable equivalent exists for a portable node build under SolidStart v2 — and every option use is documented and reasoned.

findings.issue: Nitro is pinned to a specific beta build (^3.0.260903-beta) of a version line that is still pre-stable, and the caret range cannot match the newer 3.0.261029-rc or the eventual 3.0.0 final, so the app will silently stay on a frozen beta until someone edits the range.
findings.suggestion: Track the current Nitro 3 RC (e.g. pin 3.0.261029-rc) or the final 3.0.0 once released; note that beta-pinned lockfiles also miss the security/bugfix churn the RC line is getting weekly.

findings.issue: Vite 8.3.5 is required and current-stable but only a few months past its major release; the whole stack (solidjs/start 2.1.0 from 2026-10-22, router 1.0.0, solid-js 1.9.17) is at the very newest stable edge, inheriting transitive pre-releases like h3 2.0.0-rc that @solidjs/start itself depends on (app/package-lock.json:1151).
findings.suggestion: Acceptable — this matches the framework's current stable release — but budget a maintenance pass when @solidjs/start cuts patch releases and when Nitro 3.0.0 final lands.

summary: The app is unusually conservative for its stack: every line of application code uses long-stable, documented Solid Router 1.0 / SolidStart 2 APIs, including the documented { mode: 'async' } SSR option. The only pre-stable reach is Nitro v3 (pinned to a beta), which is nonetheless the framework's own documented production-server plugin and is confined to a two-line vite.config registration plus one dependency entry. The main maintenance risk is the caret range freezing the app on a dated beta instead of the current RC/final.
